newsitem.title: USA: Breakfast ham recalled in New England - USDA.
newsitem.headline: Breakfast ham recalled in New England - USDA.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department Monday said a food processing company in New Hampshire was recalling breakfast ham because it might be contaminated with harmful bacteria.

Gould's Country Store, based in Piermont, N.H., is voluntarily recalling about 52 pounds of its "Gould's Country Smokehouse Corn Cob Smoked Breakfast Ham, Water Added," the department said. It said the ham was distributed mainly to grocery stores in the center of the state but that a small amount was also sold in Vermont.

The department said the meat may be tainted with listeria monocytogenes bacteria which can cause listeriosis, a rare but potentially serious disease. Pregnant women, children and the elderly are most suspectible to the disease, whose symptoms include nauseau, vomiting, abdominal pain, diarrhea and in some cases, flu-like symptoms such as fever, chills and headaches.
"Because of the potential hazard, we urge consumers who have purchased the suspect product to return it to the place of purchase," said Agriculture Department official Thomas Billy.

Packages of the recalled ham bear the code "33196." The department said it turned up the problem through a routine monitoring program. Consumers with questions about the recall can phone the toll-free USDA Meat and Poultry hotline at 1-800-535-4555.
